subject: Skyline renewal health & capacity sprint — commit options and ROI readout
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Erin Cole <erin@skyline.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Skyline renewal health & capacity sprint — commit options and ROI readout

Hi Erin —

Thanks again for the time last week. Attached is a short renewal health pulse and the raw token usage CSV for the last 90 days (renewal_pulse_202802.pdf, usage_breakdown_q1.csv). High-level observations: 

- Token spend is up ~42% month-over-month, driven by a new image-to-text extraction pipeline in prod (evenings peak).
- Latency P95 has slipped 80ms since the deployment change; ops traced it to an increase in longer sequence requests.
- Cost per 1k tokens improved slightly after the model switch, but gross spend is increasing.

Given these signals, we see two practical renewal paths we can offer:
1) Standard renewal with a 10% committed volume uplift (12-month term) — keeps current mix and includes a 7% discount on committed tokens.
2) Capacity-backed renewal (preferred) — 25% commit increase, guaranteed baseline latency SLA (P95) with an operational uplift plan, and volume discount of 14% plus 60k complimentary burst credits for seasonal spikes.

We put together a short ROI readout in the attached PDF showing token economics for both options and the expected payback period based on current growth.

Can you confirm which path you want us to price formally? If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min capacity sprint with our solutions engineer and your infra lead to stitch the SLA and runbook.

Best,
Priyom
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
p: (415) 555-0197
From: Erin Cole <erin@skyline.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@skyline.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Feb 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Skyline renewal health & capacity sprint — commit options and ROI readout

Thanks Priyom — got the PDF and CSV, useful summary. A couple quick clarifying points before we lock a path: 

- The spike corresponds to two product pushes: 1) an expanded inference window for context and 2) a new batch inference job running nightly that seems to be longer-sequence heavy.
- Our infra lead (Rajiv) wants the baseline SLA guarantees scoped to the production model(s) we currently use; we need to avoid a long back-and-forth on model variants.

We're broadly intrigued by option 2 (capacity-backed renewal) but need clarity on: 1) how the burst credits work, 2) precise SLA definitions, and 3) an estimate of the monthly committed spend so procurement can map it to our budget.

Can you loop in someone on the SRE/solutions side for a short tech sync? Rajiv and I are available Thursday afternoon PT.

—Erin
Head of Product, Skyline AI
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Erin Cole <erin@skyline.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Feb 2028 08:26:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Skyline renewal health & capacity sprint — commit options and ROI readout

Erin —

Great, thanks for the signal. Quick answers: 

1) Burst credits: they function as on-demand capacity applied before consuming committed tokens; you get 60k tokens/month that do not count against committed usage unless you exceed the burst pool for the billing period. They reset monthly and are designed for predictable spikes.

2) SLA: We can guarantee P95 latency on the pinned model endpoint (same model hash you have in prod) with an availability SLA of 99.5% on Dedicated pools. If a scheduled maintenance window impacts latency, we'll provide advance notice and crediting. Full SLA language will be in the term sheet.

3) Committed spend estimate: Based on the attached CSV and projected growth (conservative +20% over next 12 months), the 25% uplift maps to ~$48k/month committed spend under our current rate card before discounts. With the 14% discount and burst credits, net effective spend would be ~ $41k/mo. I'll share a formal quote.

I'll loop in Monica from CS to run the capacity sprint and Karthik from deals to draft the term sheet. Thursday 2/24 2:00pm PT works for our SRE — does that suit Rajiv?

Thanks,
Priyom
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Erin Cole <erin@skyline.ai>, Rajiv Singh <rajiv@skyline.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Feb 2028 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Skyline renewal health & capacity sprint — commit options and ROI readout

Hi Erin / Rajiv —

Quick ops notes ahead of the Thursday sync: 
- We will provision an isolated Dedicated pool for Skyline with capacity planning aligned to your peak 95th percentile token rate plus 25% buffer.
- We'll run a runbook walkthrough: cache warming, KV cache sizing, and recommended batching settings (we expect those to reduce P95 by ~30–50ms).
- For the nightly batch job, consider shifting to a staggered schedule or using our bulk ingestion API which better supports long sequences without impacting low-latency endpoints.

I'll bring a short checklist and a k8s/infra checklist for the session.

Regards,
Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
